baseline: tests/fixtures/shell-baseline (frozen phase-one migration, not the original base commit)
candidate_state: uncommitted native migration; required-app contract accepted in ADR-0001; not deployed
method: Real Bash entrypoints; release native executable; private state and cached tab; recording spool. A compiled native fixture supplies a live resident identity but does not consume requests. Baseline ps and lsappinfo are stubbed. Native process identity and cached Ghostty PID validation use macOS APIs. Every Stop request is decoded and checked before removal. Fixture processes are terminated and reaped.
scope: Hook return latency only, not end-to-end notification delivery, first uncached binding, or cold app startup. No real notifications, Apple Events, or OSC writes. Final sample run started after the build and other test processes had completed.
interpretation: In this run, cached PreToolUse median decreased by approximately 22%, and Stop median by approximately 73%, against the frozen phase-one shell implementation. This measures the full hook entrypoint under the stated cached/spool scenario, not Bash versus Swift language startup in isolation.
